papers.title: Dust growth in the early Universe: insight from the NewCluster spin-off simulation
papers.summary: We investigate dust evolution in galaxies at $z\sim5$ using a spin-off run of the \NC\ cosmological zoom-in simulation with a live two-species, two-size dust model. We find that dust evolution follows three metallicity-dependent phases. At $\log(Z/Z_\odot)<-1$, dust is dominated by stellar ejecta and produces a shallow, featureless UV extinction curve whose normalized wavelength dependence is similar to that of the Calzetti attenuation law (Phase I). At $-1\leq \log(Z/Z_\odot)<-0.5$, efficient silicate accretion drives rapid dust growth, producing silicate-rich dust and SMC-like extinction curves (Phase II). At $\log(Z/Z_\odot)\geq-0.5$, carbonaceous grain growth also becomes efficient, yielding a more balanced grain mixture and Milky-Way-like extinction curves (Phase III). In addition, local dust-to-metal ratios are strongly suppressed in regions affected by recent clustered supernova feedback, further complicating the interpretation of high-$z$ observations. Despite some successes, our galaxies lie below current observationally inferred dust masses and dust-to-metal ratios for high-redshift galaxies. The resulting depletion patterns suggest that the fixed Fe-bearing olivine composition assumed in our current dust model may be too restrictive for chemically young galaxies, and that metallicity-dependent grain compositions may be required to explain the dust content of the early Universe.

papers.title: Feeding or Fleeing: The Impact of Enhanced Early Black Hole Growth on Circumgalactic Clumps at $z > 6$
papers.summary: The circumgalactic medium (CGM) of massive high-redshift galaxies contains inflowing filamentary gas, recycled material, and feedback-driven outflows. We investigate the formation and evolution of dense CGM clumps in two cosmological zoom-in simulations of the same massive halo at $z > 6$: the fiducial Fable model and the modified Fable-SE model, which includes enhanced early black hole growth through mild super-Eddington accretion. We identify dense gas clumps in the CGM and follow their gas properties, stellar content, and radial evolution across cosmic time. At the resolution probed here, the two simulations show broadly similar distributions of clump gas mass, gas size and associated stellar mass. Instead, the clump populations differ mainly in their abundance, metallicity, and radial evolution. Fable-SE produces substantially more metal-enriched clumps, including an outward-moving population during the strong AGN-driven blow-out phase at $z \lesssim 7$. These systems are associated with disturbed HI-rich gas and relatively high gas densities, linking the increased prevalence of dense, metal-enriched CGM structures in Fable-SE to its stronger AGN-driven blow-out phase. Although inward migration dominates overall, Fable-SE also contains an outward-moving clump population during the blow-out phase, with some clumps moving beyond the virial radius. Our results therefore indicate that the distribution of dense CGM clumps around massive high-redshift galaxies reflects both filamentary accretion and feedback-driven CGM evolution, with strong early AGN activity associated with the outward migration of dense, metal-enriched gas structures containing relatively cool gas.

papers.title: Robust statistical significance for Gravitational Wave inference
papers.summary: The field of gravitational-wave data analysis heavily relies on Bayes factors to make statements about astrophysical effects in events detected by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration. This is true on an event level, for example when discussing the potential detection of precession or eccentricity, as well as on a population level. For the latter, perhaps the main limiting factor is the reliance on the output from event-level nested sampling analyses, which is known to introduce growing uncertainties and biases as the number of detections increases. In both cases, while Bayes factors are useful when comparing different models, because the underlying distribution of Bayes factors in noise is unknown, it is often not possible to use them to make quantifiable statistical statements. Their statistical meaning is also questionable in the at least $20\%$ of gravitational-wave events that contain transient noise artifacts. This paper shows that it is possible to use evidence networks, which can infer Bayes factors after learning the distinguishability between datasets, to solve all of the aforementioned problems. By being able to calculate up to $10^5$ Bayes factors per second, we can construct background distributions of Bayes factors under different signal assumptions to estimate significance. We show that the high precision achieved allows us to scale the results from up to $10^4$ events with no discernable bias on population-level quantities, while laying the foundations for a likelihood-free method that does not rely on the assumption of Gaussian and stationary noise.

papers.title: The stellar orbit distribution of 24 late-type galaxies observed by MUSE
papers.summary: We selected 24 nearby late-type galaxies from the MUSE archive with kinematic coverage extending to at least one effective radius. Stellar kinematics were extracted with the GIST pipeline using pPXF, and axisymmetric Schwarzschild models were constructed with \textsc{dynamite}. The stellar orbits of each galaxy were classified by circularity into dynamically cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating components, and we calculated the corresponding luminosity fractions of each component within $R_{\mathrm{e}}$. Our results confirm the mass-dependent trends in orbital structure previously identified from CALIFA galaxies and reproduced by IllustrisTNG. We further checked the morphology of each component and calculated the edge-on flattening of the cold, warm, and hot+CR components. With the high-quality MUSE data, we find that the dynamically warm components are common in low-mass late-type spiral galaxies, suggesting that their discs are dynamically warmer and vertically thicker than those of more massive spirals. We regard this as a tentative result, given the limited sample size.

papers.title: The first mass peak of merging black holes from core binding energies and jet-driven explosions
papers.summary: We show that the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) can qualitatively reproduce the shape of the black hole (BH) mass distribution observed by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA and quantitatively reproduce the peak around $M_{p1} \simeq 10 M_\odot$. To show this, we construct a toy model that captures the JJEM physics that explodes all massive stars, even when BHs form. According to the JJEM, BHs form when the star's binding energy is large, implying a massive progenitor with initial mass $M_i \gtrsim 25 M_\odot$, and when jets are launched along a fixed axis, implying a rapidly rotating pre-collapse stellar core. In this case, the jets are launched along the core's angular momentum and are inefficient at removing mass near the equatorial plane; when the stellar binding energy is large, a large fraction of the equatorial mass is accreted to form the BH. The toy model includes two parameters: the threshold binding energy in the core for BH formation and the jet opening angle along the poles. Although our finding is encouraging for the JJEM, future hydrodynamical simulations must determine the exact condition for BH formation in the JJEM and the BH mass.

papers.title: Tidal disruption or plunge: the role of neutron star internal structure in black hole-neutron star mergers
papers.summary: The outcome of black hole--neutron star (BHNS) mergers is studied using a general-relativistic mass-shedding condition in the Kerr spacetime, which determines the tidal-disruption radius from the mass ratio, the black hole (BH) spin, the neutron star (NS) compactness, and the ratio of central to average density, $\eta=\frac{\rho_{c}}{\bar\rho}$. Comparing this radius with the innermost stable circular orbit, we map the boundary between tidal disruption and plunge for two relativistic mean-field equations of state (EOSs) and for an ensemble of about $10^4$ agnostic EOSs spanning the current uncertainty in the NS radius. We find that the disruption threshold is set mainly by the compactness, but NSs with the same compactness and different $\eta$ can have different outcomes. Using the tidal disruption radius, we construct a remnant-mass model calibrated against 70 numerical-relativity simulations, which reproduces the remnant mass with an accuracy comparable to existing fits. Applying the disruption criterion and the remnant model to GW200105, GW200115, and the candidate BHNS event GW230529, we find that GW200105 and GW200115 are consistent with a direct plunge. GW230529 lies close to the disruption threshold and may have undergone marginal disruption, leaving only a low-mass remnant.

papers.title: VERITAS Limits on Dark Matter Annihilation in the Galactic Center Halo
papers.summary: Well-motivated models of particle dark matter predict its self-annihilation into Standard Model end states, which may be detected by particle detectors or telescopes. We conduct an indirect dark matter search using gamma rays detected by the VERITAS telescope from within $2^\circ$ of the Galactic Center. A template-based approach is used for background estimation, increasing our sensitivity to sources of gamma-ray emission with spatial extents comparable to the $3.5^\circ$ VERITAS field of view. The analysis benefits from data taken exclusively at large zenith angles, which results in an increased effective area at energies above ~1 TeV, compared to small zenith angle observations. No significant gamma-ray signal is observed in the search region, resulting in upper limits on the end-state-dependent dark matter annihilation cross sections. Cross sections as low as $\langle \sigma_\text{ann} v\rangle = 1.77\times 10^{-25} \text{ cm}^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$ are excluded at 95% confidence assuming complete annihilation into $\tau^+ \tau^-$, an Einasto profile, and a dark matter mass of 1 TeV.

papers.title: Energy-Dependent Hard X-Ray QPP Modulation in M- and X-Class Solar Flares Observed by Aditya-L1/HEL1OS
papers.summary: Quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) in solar-flare hard X-ray (HXR) emission provide observational constraints on the temporal variability of flare energy release and energetic-electron production. In our previous study, we established a systematic catalogue of HXR QPPs in HEL1OS observations of X-class solar flares, identifying statistically significant pulsations in 25 of 34 events with sufficient data quality (S. Rajkapoor Kanaujiya et al. 2026). Here, we extend this investigation by comparing the energy dependence of the modulation depth of QPPs in M- and X-class flares across four HEL1OS energy channels spanning 8-20 keV. The comparison comprises 18 M-class events and the X-class sample from our previous study, with the number of available measurements varying between energy channels. In both flare populations, the modulation depth increases with photon energy. For M-class flares, it rises from approximately 2.3% at 8-11 keV to 13.2% at 17-20 keV, whereas for X-class flares increase from approximately 1.0% to 3.1%. The stronger increase towards higher energies in the M-class sample constitutes the principal observational contrast. These results demonstrate an energy-dependent increase in the relative amplitude of HXR QPPs in both populations and motivate a systematic statistical assessment of whether their energy-dependent modulation-depth distributions differ. The comparison provides a basis for constraining models of QPP generation and the modulation of energetic-electron emission during solar flares.

papers.title: A MUSE and MeerKAT study of dynamics and star formation in HCG 16
papers.summary: Context. Hickson Compact Groups (HCGs) present an ideal environment for studying galaxy interactions. HCG 16 is a group of five galaxies in an intermediate stage of evolution (Phase 2), with several members displaying signs of interaction, including distorted morphologies, tidal features, and enhanced star formation rates. Aims. We aim to better understand the evolution of HCG 16 and its member galaxies, focusing on the relationship between neutral hydrogen and star formation, while reconstructing the interaction history of the group. Methods. We analysed MUSE data processed with pyPipe3D to extract H$\alpha$ images and stellar population synthesis results, and reduced MeerKAT data to produce a high-resolution HI cube. We examined the structure and dynamics of the H$\alpha$ and HI lines in both 2D and 3D, and produced spatially resolved star formation histories to compare the inner and outer parts of the galaxies. Results. We identify a major star formation episode in HCG 16 beginning ~400-500 Myr ago, coinciding with the passage of NGC 848 close to the other member galaxies, and that continued at least until 50-60 Myr ago in some galaxies. The HI distribution is highly perturbed in the group, although HCG 16a retains a nearly regular disk, while HCG 16b has associated H$\alpha$ tails. Conclusions. The passage of NGC 848 probably activated star formation in HCG 16, but cannot by itself explain the current starburst activity in HCG 16c and 16d. The evolution of the group is better explained by multiple interactions among its members than by a single strong encounter.

papers.title: Preparation of a celestial field for precise VLBI observations of the JUICE spacecraft: a test case of the Venus flyby
papers.summary: The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer mission, launched in 2023, is on its way to the Jovian system, to arrive in 2031. The Planetary Radio Interferometry and Doppler Experiment performs radio astronomical observations of the spacecraft already in its interplanetary cruise phase. Since the sky density of potential compact radio sources suitable as phase-reference calibrators in very long baseline interferometry observations is low, densifying the celestial reference frame along the Ecliptic is an essential task in support of JUICE. In preparation for the JUICE gravity assist manoeuvre at Venus in August 2025, to support the accurate reconstruction of the spacecraft state vector, we selected in-beam calibrator source candidates along the JUICE trajectory. Additionally, we attempted to link known nearby bright compact reference sources from the Radio Fundamental Catalog to the International Celestial Reference Frame. We performed nodding-style phase-referencing VLBI observations with the European VLBI Network at 8.4GHz, targeting nine in-beam calibrator candidate and three RFC sources in the celestial vicinity of JUICE's trajectory during its Venus flyby. We linked their positions to nearby ICRF sources by means of relative astrometry. Four of the ICC targets and all RFC sources were detected and imaged with the EVN, and their coordinates determined with typically sub-mas precision. Although none of the targeted ICC sources proved suitable as VLBI phase-reference calibrators because of being too faint or resolved, their newly-determined positions and flux densities could in principle be used to verify the detection of the spacecraft at the time of the actual flyby around Venus. During the detailed analysis of the ICC targets, we found that the structure of one of them, J0843+1826 is resolved on mas scale, and the other one, J0843+1814 is a young radio galaxy, likely a member of a cluster.

papers.title: Recent advances in numerical modeling of solar inertial modes
papers.summary: Inertial modes are low-frequency global oscillations in rotating fluids, restored by the Coriolis force. Long-term observations of horizontal flows on the solar surface have led to the detection of various inertial modes on the Sun, opening a new window into the structure and dynamics of the solar interior. Here, we focus on recent advances in the theoretical modeling of solar inertial modes within a purely hydrodynamic framework, leaving magnetohydrodynamic effects beyond the scope of this review. Because the low-frequency oscillations of a differentially rotating spherical shell depend sensitively on the rotation profile and the properties of the medium, they are primarily studied using numerical models. We first summarize how linear eigenmode analyses have enabled the identification and classification of different families of inertial modes observed on the Sun, and how these models reveal the strong diagnostic potential of inertial modes for probing poorly constrained parameters in the deep convection zone, such as turbulent viscosity and superadiabaticity. The amplitudes of linearly stable modes can be estimated from their response to stochastic forcing, whereas those of linearly unstable modes must be determined using nonlinear numerical modeling. We further discuss the possible dynamical roles of large-amplitude inertial modes in transporting heat and angular momentum in the Sun. By clarifying what has been established and what remains uncertain, this review provides a framework for interpreting current observations and guiding future theoretical developments in this rapidly evolving field.

papers.title: Mapping cluster angular momentum with the rotational kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect
papers.summary: Galaxy clusters carry angular momentum. If the intracluster gas rotates coherently, the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect imprints a dipole on the microwave sky centered on the cluster. We show that microwave maps alone can be used to reconstruct a noisy vector field tracing the projected angular momentum of the ionized gas. We present an optimal multifrequency matched filter (MMF) that isolates the rotational kSZ (rkSZ) signal from the much larger miscentered thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect, cosmic microwave, and infrared background contributions, improving on both real-space oriented stacking and matched filtering of maps cleaned with full-sky multifrequency weights. For the rkSZ profile, we introduce a simple model for coherent intracluster gas rotation and validate it against TNG-Cluster and TNG300-1. The model consists of differentially rotating concentric shells with constant equatorial tangential velocity, characterized by a mass- and redshift-indepedent tangential-to-circular velocity ratio of $v_{\rm tan}/V_{c,200c}=0.18$. Using this model, we forecast single-cluster signal-to-noise (SNR) as a function of mass and redshift for Simons Observatory; cross-correlation with an external catalog of rotation proxies yields a cumulative detection SNR. For an idealized mass-limited catalog with perfectly known spin directions, the cumulative SNR of our optimal MMF reaches $\approx 53$, $25$, and $6$ when including all clusters above $\log_{10}(M_{200c}/M_\odot)>14$, 14.5, and 15, respectively. This work provides a practical framework for CMB measurements of intracluster gas rotation, with applications to the rotational contribution to non-thermal pressure in cluster mass calibration, as well as spin alignments and clustering biases.

papers.title: Channelled versus Isotropic Accretion of Galaxy Groups onto Clusters: Kinematics, Spin Alignment, and Assembly Bias
papers.summary: Galaxy clusters grow by accreting groups from the cosmic web, but whether the route of infall (along a cluster-connected filament or from the open field) imprints a group's kinematics, spin, and orbit remains unmeasured at scale. We classify $212{,}704$ group-cluster infall pairs across $27{,}029$ clusters in the $(1\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Gpc})^3$ MDPL2 simulation into primary (cluster-connected), secondary (tributary), primary-outskirt, and isotropic channels using DisPerSE filaments. (i) In both channelled classes, group spin axes lie mainly parallel to the filament below a `spin-flip' mass and perpendicular above it, $\log_{10} M_\mathrm{flip}\;[h^{-1}\,M_{\odot}] = 13.07$ and $13.12$, a $0.05$-dex offset consistent with zero, lying $1.3-1.4$ dex above the field, while isotropic groups show no flip; $M_\mathrm{flip}$ stays radially flat out to $7\,R_{200}$. (ii) Within the primary class $M_\mathrm{flip}$ rises with the linear mass density of the host filament, from $12.96$ (thin tendrils) to $13.44$ (dense bridges); matching group mass, cluster mass and distance keeps the rise positive but leaves its size uncertain ($0.07-0.58$ dex). (iii) Isotropic groups fall below random alignment at $2\,R_{200}$ ($41$ per cent within $60^\circ$, a $4.3\sigma$ deficit). Primary groups show $85$ per cent velocity-filament alignment at $2\,R_{200}$, and isotropic groups infall $150-180\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ faster, and more radially, out to $5\,R_{200}$. At matched distance isotropic groups are therefore predicted to reach orbital pericentres up to $10$ per cent smaller than primary groups, whose smaller pooled pericentres reflect only their proximity to the cluster. The topological route of accretion, and within it the host filament's linear density, shapes how groups enter clusters, testable with wide-area spectroscopic surveys.

papers.title: Analysis of Multi-Wavelength Data for 30 Galactic Emission-Line Stars with Dusty Envelopes
papers.summary: We selected 30 stars with V-band brightnesses of 11-16 mag, visual color-indices B-V of approximately 1.3 mag or less, and large near-IR color-indices (J-H and H-K of approximately 0.7 mag or greater) to search for the presence of the B[e] phenomenon. Spectroscopic observations confirmed the presence of emission lines previously detected in 11 stars of the sample and revealed them in 4 other stars for the first time. Spectral energy distributions (SEDs) in the optical and IR spectral regions were analyzed and compared with theoretical SEDs. The fundamental parameters were estimated using the SED fits corrected for the interstellar and circumstellar (CS) extinction and Gaia DR3 distance measurements. Properties of 14 objects previously classified as pre-main-sequence stars were reevaluated. The B[e] phenomenon was found in 16 objects, most of which exhibit observed properties of FS CMa type objects, a still small group of Galactic stars or binary systems with predominantly hot CS dust. Properties of 2 objects (IRAS 06237+0020 and IRAS 19156-0935) are consistent with those of Proto-Planetary Nebulae at early phases of this evolutionary stage. The nature and evolutionary status of 11 sample objects remain uncertain and require further investigation.

papers.title: Identifying narrow-band mutual coupling resonances in SKA-low stations using frequency-independent current basis functions
papers.summary: Mutual coupling between closely spaced elements in aperture arrays introduces narrow-band spectral features in the Embedded Element Patterns (EEPs), threatening measurements of the 21-cm power spectrum with instruments such as SKA-low. We detail a method to identify such features through the construction of frequency-independent current basis functions, utilising a singular value decomposition of frequency-dependent basis functions. We demonstrate the method on a three-element linear array and full pseudo-random station of SKA log-periodic antennas and examine the current power induced by mutual coupling. For the pseudo-random layout station we note many narrow-band resonance features, including strong resonances at 50.8~MHz and 83.6~MHz, where the coupled power on the passive antennas can approach or exceed that of the excited antenna. Simulated delay power spectra for the SKA-low core show that observing in frequency bands including resonance features causes large foreground leakage within the delay power spectra, obscuring the EoR window. For the pseudo-random layout station with SKALA4.0 we identify two significant frequency bands from 59.2--76.2~MHz and 84.2--103.3~MHz which are free of contamination from current resonances, preserving the EoR window in these frequency ranges.

papers.title: Four-hundred Very Metal-poor Stars Studied with LAMOST and Subaru. IV. Heavy Element Enhanced Stars
papers.summary: We perform a homogeneous analysis of 82 heavy-element-enhanced metal-poor stars from the\\ LAMOST/Subaru sample, including 64 $r$-process-enhanced stars, 2 limited-$r$ stars, and 16 stars exhibiting significant or moderate carbon enhancement (comprising 9 $s$-process-enhanced, 2 $r$-process-enhanced, 2 $r$/$s$, and 3 $r$+$s$ stars). Systematic differences in $\mathrm{[X/Eu]}$ between $r$-I and $r$-II stars, together with their distinct dynamical properties, suggest that $r$-II stars likely formed in low-mass dwarf galaxies where contamination from additional nucleosynthetic channels was minimal. We have also discovered a number of peculiar objects. We identify an extremely metal-poor $r$-II star, J1158+0734 ($\mathrm{[Fe/H]}$ = -2.93), whose enhanced Zn abundance ($\mathrm{[Zn/Fe]}$ = +0.67) is best explained by yields from a high-energy, massive core-collapse supernova. The surface abundances of $s$-process-enhanced stars exhibit pronounced dispersion, consistent with enrichment from AGB progenitors with diverse properties. Notably, one star, J2256+0215, reveals compelling evidence for additional evolutionary mixing, as indicated by its unusually low carbon abundance ($\mathrm{[C/Fe]}$ = +0.08) and extremely low $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 2.33. Additionally, we identify 3 $r$+$s$ stars whose abundance patterns reveal combined contributions from both the $r$- and $s$-processes. We further propose a modified diagnostic scheme for the identification of CEMP-$r$+$s$ stars, defined as: -0.2 $\leqslant$ $\mathrm{[La/Nd]}$ $\leqslant$ 0.2 and -0.5 $\leqslant$ $\mathrm{[Eu/Nd]}$ $\leqslant$ 0.0.

papers.title: Nine new eclipsing accreting ultracompact white dwarf binaries from the Zwicky Transient Facility
papers.summary: Accreting ultracompact white dwarf binaries (accreting UCBs) transfer helium-rich material at orbital periods below about 65 min, and mainly divide into hydrogen-free AM CVn binaries and helium cataclysmic variables. Eclipsing systems are of particular value: they allow the component masses and radii to be measured independently of any model, the most direct test of the proposed formation channels, and they form a sample with a simple, well-understood selection function. Only 21 eclipsing accreting white dwarf UCBs have been published. We aim to enlarge the sample of eclipsing accreting UCBs available for detailed characterisation. We searched the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) light curves of Gaia-selected candidates and of ZTF-selected dwarf novae for short-period eclipse signals using a box least-squares period search. Identification spectra of nine systems were obtained with LRIS on the Keck I telescope. We present nine new discoveries and re-analyse the four systems first reported by Khalil et al. (2024). Eclipses are detected directly in the survey photometry of all 13 systems, which have orbital periods between 26.0 and 65.0 min and median ZTF magnitudes $g = 18.7-21.5$. Ten are consistent with being AM CVn binaries, and two are likely helium cataclysmic variables (of which one may host a high-state disc). The remaining system, ZTF J2116+2446, shows only hydrogen lines, making it the shortest-period UCB with hydrogen but no detected helium; it may have evolved from a white dwarf-brown dwarf binary. The nine new systems increase the number of published eclipsing accreting UCBs from 21 to 30. Because they are eclipsing, they are immediately available for the high-speed photometric modelling that yields model-independent masses and radii, to be presented in future work, including for the three hydrogen-rich systems that are key tests of the evolved cataclysmic-variable channel.

papers.title: SDSS-V LVM: Mapping of plasma temperatures in the Lagoon Nebula reveals the origin of long-standing chemical abundance discrepancies
papers.summary: Knowing the chemical composition of interstellar gas is essential for understanding the chemical evolution of galaxies. Ionized nebulae provide key laboratories for this purpose, where chemical abundances are commonly derived from emission lines of heavy ions such as doubly ionized oxygen, $O^{++}$. Abundances can be inferred either from collisionally excited lines (CELs) or from recombination lines (RLs). However, for more than 80 years, the former have yielded systematically lower abundances than the latter. We map this ''abundance discrepancy'' using the first spatially resolved integral field unit (IFU) observations of $O^{++}$ RLs and CELs across a Milky Way H II region: the Lagoon Nebula (a.k.a. M8). Modeling the data using a plasma temperature perturbation model, we present unequivocal evidence that electron temperature ($T_e$) fluctuations drive the abundance discrepancy in M8. We find a tight correlation between the abundance discrepancy and the difference between $T_e$ derived from the classical CEL method and a hybrid RL/CEL approach. We identify this Te discrepancy as an observational proxy for the amplitude of the thermal fluctuations, providing a new, direct way to quantify their effect on nebular abundances. The correlation constrains the mean electron temperature of the gas. Adopting this mean temperature reconciles CEL and RL abundances, effectively eliminating the abundance discrepancy.

papers.title: Can the $\sim 5$ kpc starburst ring in MW create eROSITA bubbles?
papers.summary: eROSITA bubbles (eRBs) in our Galaxy are thought to be due to the energy injection by the central star-forming region or the central Super Massive Black Hole. Identifying the origin of these bubbles is crucial in constraining the origin of the Fermi Bubbles and the nature of the Galactic feedback. However, some recent opinions suggest that the eRBs may not even have been produced by any central source, but rather a result of a star-formation ring at $R\sim 5$ kpc. In this letter, we perform detailed hydrodynamic simulations to refute that claim and show that such a ring of star formation alone is not able to produce the symmetric eROSITA bubbles - one needs a compact energy injection from the Galactic Center to produce these bubbles. Our study, therefore, suggests that the eROSITA bubbles truly represent the nuclear outflow from our Galaxy.

papers.title: KM3-230213A: The Highest-Energy Cosmic Neutrino
papers.summary: High-energy neutrinos provide a unique probe of the most extreme non-thermal processes in the Universe. The detection of the ultra-high-energy neutrino event KM3-230213A by the KM3NeT neutrino telescope, with an inferred parent-neutrino energy of O(10^17 eV), represents a major step forward in neutrino astronomy. In this review, we summarize the main properties of the event and discuss its interpretation within different astrophysical and cosmological scenarios, including active galactic nuclei, transient sources, and cosmogenic neutrinos, highlighting the role of multi-messenger constraints. Despite extensive follow-up observations, no unambiguous electromagnetic counterpart has been identified, and the event remains in tension with the absence of comparable detections in other experiments. This situation leaves open the possibility of more complex source scenarios or contributions from physics beyond the Standard Model. We also discuss the implications for the ultra-high-energy neutrino landscape and the prospects for future observations with next-generation detectors. KM3-230213A provides a unique opportunity to probe particle acceleration and neutrino production at energies far beyond the reach of terrestrial experiments.

papers.title: Extracting non-Gaussian information of line-intensity maps with weighted skew spectra
papers.summary: The bispectrum of line-intensity maps carries cosmological and astrophysical information beyond the power spectrum, but its large data vector hampers the analysis of survey data. Skew spectra address this by compressing the bispectrum into a handful of power-spectrum-like observables, cross-spectra of the observed field with filtered squares of it. We present the first application of optimally weighted skew spectra to line-intensity mapping of galaxy-hosted emission, where all clustering and shot-noise terms are luminosity weighted and the mean intensity is unknown. We perform idealized real-space Fisher forecasts for a SPHEREx-like survey of H$\alpha$ emission at $0.2 \lesssim z \lesssim 4.6$, in its deep fields and in a noisier all-sky configuration. First, the compression carries over to intensity maps: on perturbative scales and for a fixed redshift evolution of the emitters, four skew spectra, one of them matched to the shot noise, recover the bispectrum constraints on biases, shot noise and cosmological parameters to within a few percent. Second, the joint analysis of the power spectrum and the skew spectra measures the ratios of the second-order biases to the linear bias in each redshift bin. Within a bin the biases are degenerate with the unknown mean intensity, but their ratios are not, so their redshift evolution is measured without a model for the emitters. For emission that depends on halo mass alone, these ratios are determined by luminosity-weighted averages of the halo biases, so their evolution can test the halo-emission connection, including dependence on assembly history or environment. The bias ratios are not accessible to the tree-level real-space power spectrum alone. At $z \lesssim 3$ an all-sky SPHEREx-like configuration can detect departures of order $0.1$ in the bias ratios at $3\sigma$, while deeper fields perform better in the highest-redshift bins.

papers.title: Seven Years of TESS Precovery Observations of the Dwarf-planet Candidate 2026 ED$_{138}$
papers.summary: The trans-Neptunian object 2026 ED$_{138}$ was announced in 2026 October as the first dwarf-planet candidate in our solar system discovered by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) observed it in five month-long sectors between 2019 and 2026, four of them before its discovery. We subtract every Gaia DR3 star from these crowded full-frame images with the TESS-Gaia Light Curve (TGLC) package, then remove static residuals with a running median. Stacking the images along its predicted path detects 2026 ED$_{138}$ in all five sectors at 5-21$\sigma$, and at 34$\sigma$ combined. The TESS positions alone confirm the JPL orbit, and its brightness is consistent with the 0.08 mag fading expected from its increasing distance and changing phase angle.

papers.title: The dark surface of (163693) Atira and implications for inner-Earth asteroid origins
papers.summary: We compare the physical properties of inner-Earth asteroid (163693) Atira with the NEOMOD3 population model. Its radar-derived diameter of 4.9 km and absolute magnitude H$_V\simeq$16.4 imply a geometric albedo of p$_V\sim$0.02. Photometry with the Astrophysical Research Consortium 3.5-m telescope and ARCTIC yields g-r=0.49$\pm$0.03, r-i=0.20$\pm$0.02, i-z=0.02$\pm$0.03, a$^\ast$=$-0.05\pm0.03$, and a g-to-i spectral slope of 3.4$\pm$0.9$\%$/100 nm. The photometric reflectance favors a provisional X-type classification; combined with the low albedo, it supports a Tholen P-type interpretation. NEOMOD3 assigns an approximately 66$\%$ probability of delivery through inner Main Belt channels and 26$\%$ to central and outer Main Belt channels. Atira's NEOMOD3 albedo-category probabilities are $0.07\pm0.02$, $0.64\pm0.04$, and $0.29\pm0.04$ for p$_V<$0.1, 0.1$\leq$p$_V<$0.3, and p$_V\geq$0.3, respectively. Across 38 inner-Earth objects, including Atira and 'Ayl\'o'chaxnim, inner Main Belt delivery generally dominates, and intermediate albedo is favored for 33 objects. Atira therefore represents an uncommon low-albedo outcome, compatible with delivery of dark material from the inner Main Belt or more distant primitive populations. Further characterization of inner-Earth asteroids will test whether current population models reproduce their compositional diversity.

papers.title: What kinds of strong star--black-hole encounters in AGN disks occur, and how often?
papers.summary: Disks surrounding active galactic nuclei contain many stars and black holes, which will inevitably encounter one another. The outcome of these encounters depends on how closely and how rapidly the bodies meet. Extending previous studies, we account for initial relative velocities seeded by stochastic effects in the disk; incorporate a strong-encounter cross-section accounting for single- and binary-mediated interactions computed via direct two-body (Hill) or three-body (isolated) interactions; and present a repeated-encounter model accounting both for energy loss due to stellar encounters as well as the SMBH tidal field. We convolve our encounter model with a parametric family of natal stellar and binary populations, focused on varying binary fraction and period distribution. In our fiducial disk model, even though single-single interactions supply most encounters, binary-mediated interactions supply 68% of collisions; most encounters are well-approximated as parabolic; and stochastically-driven relative velocities are comparatively substantial and driven by gravitational perturbations from disk fluctuations and neighboring bodies. Our tools are ready to use in downstream applications, including several easily-expressed semianalytic approximations to key interaction phenomena.

papers.title: Temporal regularization of petal modes in SCAO systems: The Soft-Limiter approach
papers.summary: Extremely large telescopes (ELTs) rely on segmented mirrors and thick support structures that fragment the pupil. In single-conjugate AO (SCAO), this produces differential pistons, or petal modes. The Pyramid Wavefront Sensor (PWFS), baseline for ANDES, MICADO, HARMONI, and GMT-NGSAO, has poor sensitivity to these modes in the visible under realistic residual turbulence. We aim to prevent the "Island Effect", where poorly observed differential pistons accumulate and degrade the PSF, without compromising continuous-mode correction. We propose the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) Soft-Limiter, a deterministic, lightweight controller combining a subspace MMSE estimator derived from von K\'arm\'an priors with a continuous temporal regularization. It acts as a leaky integrator applied only to the relative petal degrees of freedom. End-to-end SPECULA simulations of ELT/ANDES show that, while a classical integrator loses lock and wanders across multiple fringes at seeing $\ge 1.0''$, the MMSE Soft-Limiter confines the differential piston within a single fringe over the $0.6-1.2''$ range. It bounds the petal excursion and its science-band impact under severe turbulence, while keeping optimal continuous-mode correction at good seeing, without the Strehl penalty of spatial mitigation such as Edge Actuator Coupling. We derive and verify the operating window for the leakage gain, $g \lesssim g_{\mathrm{eff}}/\pi$: below it, the fast loop retains genuine physical steps up to $\lambda_{WFS}/2$ with a small droop. This maintains a stable modulo-$\lambda_{WFS}$ wavefront on the fast sensor, letting a slower phasing sensor resolve integer ambiguities. As the window narrows with turbulence, its boundaries cross near $1.0''$ seeing; beyond this, retaining physical discontinuities becomes the sole responsibility of the phasing channel, a key design driver for segmented ELTs.

papers.title: Model-Based Retrieval of Four Years of JWST/NIRCam Wavefronts
papers.summary: The fidelity of data recovered by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) depends on precise monitoring of the mirror segments' surfaces and alignment. To this end, every few days the observatory takes pairs of defocused images of a reference star with its NIRCam instrument; a closed-source phase retrieval package is then employed to infer the wavefront. We here present camino (Computational Aberration Modelling and Inference for NIRCam Observations), an open-source algorithm to model NIRCam built in JAX using the differentiable Fresnel optics code dLUX and regularised maximum likelihood inference that has been conditioned on the entire archive of NIRCam wavefront sensing data. We typically improve the reduced chi-squared in fits to the defocused data from 60-65 to 12-13. We reconstruct the wavefront history of JWST from the beginning of science operations to early 2026. This open source implementation operates in parallel to the current STScI phase retrieval algorithm, allowing access by the broader scientific community to high-accuracy wavefront estimation and enabling its direct integration into science-analysis workflows. This represents a major step towards the ultimate goal of predictive calibration methods based on physics-based forward modelling, obviating the need for time-consuming observation of contemporaneous dedicated reference stars.

papers.title: Theoretical Consistency and Observational Constraints on Entropic Cosmology
papers.summary: Recent DESI DR2 results suggest that dark energy may evolve with time, which motivates a re-examination of entropic cosmology. In this work, we study three representative entropic models, denoted as Models A, B, and C, corresponding to the driving terms $H^2$, $H^2+\dot H$, and $H^2+\dot H+H^4$, respectively. We establish a general framework for entropic cosmology and examine these models through early universe consistency, the Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture (TCC), and the realization of Quintom-B crossing. We constrain these models using the Pantheon+ sample, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, and compare their fits to the data. For Model C, we adopt a first-order perturbative treatment in the full data analysis to maintain numerical stability in the presence of the higher-order term. We find that Model A is the simplest among the three models, but it is difficult to make it compatible with both early universe consistency and the TCC condition. Model B, which includes a derivative correction term, shows a small difference in the fit to observational data compared to Model A, and is more consistent with the theoretical constraints. Model C includes more correction terms, but does not provide a better fit to the data. The parameter region favored by observations does not fully overlap with that preferred by theoretical consistency, which suggests that entropic cosmology may require further development to achieve a self-consistent description across different cosmic epochs.

papers.title: Celia: Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions
papers.summary: Cosmological hydrodynamical simulations connect observed galaxies to cosmology and the physics of galaxy formation. Each simulation is expensive, and different codes model galaxy formation in different ways. We present Celia (Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions), a self-supervised foundation model that maps catalogs of subhalos and their galaxy properties to an embedding vector for the purposes of compression and organization of astrophysical and large-scale structure information. Celia is pretrained without parameter labels on the IllustrisTNG, SIMBA and Astrid suites of CAMELS and their N-body counterparts, by reconstructing masked subhalo properties and predicting the representations of a teacher network. Simple linear models fitted to the embeddings recover $\Omega_{\mathrm m}$ with $R^2=0.999$, and $\sigma_8$ and both supernova-feedback amplitudes with $R^2\geq0.97$, in all three suites. The embeddings translate well to out-of-distribution simulations such as Swift-EAGLE, a code that Celia never saw. A linear model fitted on the three training codes predicts its $\Omega_{\mathrm m}$ with a correlation coefficient $r=0.985$, and linear models fitted on 20 labeled simulations reach $r\geq0.94$ for $\Omega_{\mathrm m}$, $\sigma_8$ and a supernova-feedback amplitude. We decompose the variation among the simulations of each suite into principal components of the embedding, and simple power laws of the simulation parameters describe the leading components. Celia gives simulated galaxy catalogs a shared coordinate system for simulation-based inference, emulation, the comparison of galaxy-formation models, the detection of physical degeneracies and the discovery of new astrophysical probes.

papers.title: A compact NH$_2$D source without NH$_3$ counterpart in the S187 high-mass star-forming region
papers.summary: Our goal is to investigate a so far only tentatively detected compact NH$_2$D source devoid of a notable NH$_3$ counterpart, located rather close to the luminous IRAS 01202+6133 source (the projected distance is $\lesssim$0.3 pc) in the S187 high-mass star-forming region. A high ammonia deuteration in such an environment is unusual. We performed observations of this area with the 20-m OSO radio telescope in several frequency ranges from $\sim$72 to $\sim$112 GHz. The area was mapped at the lower frequencies while at the higher frequencies only the position of the NH$_2$D emission peak was observed. The data were analyzed using non-LTE modeling. The data confirm a compact NH$_2$D source with a size of $\lesssim$0.2 pc. In addition, emission from about 20 molecules was detected, but only the DCO$^+$(1-0) peak coincides with the NH$_2$D clump. The clump is not associated with any known astronomical source or an NH$_3$ emission peak but the dust continuum map shows an enhancement at approximately the same position. The gas kinetic temperature derived from various indicators is $\sim$20-30 K, which possibly characterizes the surrounding material. The intrinsic NH$_2$D line width ($\sim$0.4 km/s) implies a clump with subsonic or transonic turbulence. The ortho/para NH$_2$D line intensity ratio is consistent with an abundance ratio of 3, expected from the spin statistics. The NH$_2$D/NH$_3$ abundance ratio may be $\sim$1. In general, the data hint at a compact cold gravitationally stable dense core within the warm environment, which may represent pristine material. However this picture still needs a verification with observations at a higher angular resolution.

papers.title: From photons to neutrinos : Advancing multi-messenger modeling with Gammapy
papers.summary: In recent years, several astrophysical objects have been identified as potential multi-messenger photon-neutrino emitters. New instruments dedicated to the study of these two messengers have been and are still being built, achieving unprecedented sensitivity. This observational improvement increases the need for more sophisticated and precise analysis tools. Multi-wavelength and multi-messenger data fitting is crucial to constrain astrophysical models of particle acceleration and radiation mechanisms at work in these extreme environments. In this contribution, we present a novel framework dedicated to multi-wavelength and multi-messenger modeling, built within the open-source software Gammapy. The framework enables data analysis from optical up to very-high-energy gamma rays, and fitting physical models directly to instrumental counts in these wavebands, without the need of computing flux points. Focusing on blazars as a first example of a multi-messenger candidate, we showcase the performance of this tool in constraining multi-wavelength emission models, and how it reduces fitting biases. We show the results of a leptonic model that can be fitted on the fly, due to the short computing time needed. For more computing-intensive emission codes, we explore a grid-fitting approach. We evaluate the performance of the new fitting tool and present its first application to leptonic modeling of blazars. By fitting directly on photon and neutrino events, this novel approach will enable, for the first time, statistically sound constraints on the physics of multi-messenger sources.

papers.title: A Candidate Binary Microlensing Event in the 2018 Gamma-Ray Flare of 3C 279
papers.summary: The April 2018 gamma-ray flare of the flat-spectrum radio quasar 3C~279 exhibited sharp peaks within a broader outburst. Its rapid substructure was previously attributed to magnetic reconnection. Motivated by its distinctive temporal profile within our comparison sample of bright blazar flares and its resemblance to caustic-crossing features in optical microlensing events, we investigate a finite-source binary-microlensing interpretation. A jointly fitted model of binary-lens magnification, a smooth intrinsic flare, and Gaussian-process variability reproduces the principal double-peaked structure of the GeV light curve. The adopted local solution has a binary mass ratio of $q\simeq0.098$ and an Einstein timescale of $t_{\rm E}\simeq0.327$~d. The absolute lens mass and projected source radius depend on the lens distance and relative proper motion. The fitted geometry can correspond to a Galactic planetary-mass binary or an intervening stellar or substellar system, with different physical source sizes in each case. We present binary microlensing as a testable interpretation of this event, with the finite-source structure offering a potential probe of the compact GeV-emitting region.

papers.title: Toward a Complete Interpretation of Global 21 cm Absorption Signals Using the Radio CMB
papers.summary: The global 21 cm signal is among the most direct probes of cosmic dawn, encoding information about when the first stars formed and how efficiently they heated their surroundings. However, such measurements are limited by bright Galactic foregrounds, ionospheric effects, and instrumental systematics. Even a confident detection would face a further obstacle: the brightness temperature depends on the spin temperature of the gas and the temperature of the radio background only through a single combination, so anomalous signals such as the EDGES (Bowman et al. 2018) absorption trough admit both cold gas and excess radio background interpretations. Recently, Holder et al. 2026 showed that resonant 21 cm absorption by high-redshift neutral hydrogen imprints an excess optical depth on CMB anisotropies at radio wavelengths, which depends on the spin temperature alone. Here we propose combining a measurement of the CMB hydrogen optical depth with the global signal to break this degeneracy, isolating the radio background temperature without the need for astrophysical modelling. Forecasting four interferometric configurations, we find that a compact $55 \times 55$ array of 6 m dishes observing for 4000 hours can establish an EDGES-like optical depth at $4.2\sigma$, while fiducial cosmic dawn histories require roughly an order of magnitude more collecting area. This constitutes a model-independent route to interpreting any global 21 cm detection.

papers.title: Polarization and Burst Properties of the Repeating FRB~20240209A in a Quiescent Elliptical Host
papers.summary: We report polarimetric observations of the repeating fast radio burst (FRB) source FRB 20240209A with the Green Bank Telescope at L band and 800 MHz. This source has previously been associated with a quiescent elliptical galaxy with a mass-weighted stellar age of approximately 11 Gyr. We detected three bursts, and the brightest burst resolves into eight components that drift toward lower frequencies. The bursts have mutually consistent rotation measures (RMs), and the small extragalactic RM agrees with the low RM predicted from the small host-galaxy dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}_\mathrm{host}$). The linear polarization fraction decreases toward lower frequencies within the brightest burst, consistent with depolarization by an RM scatter of $\sigma_\mathrm{RM}\simeq3.5$ rad m$^{-2}$. This RM scatter is comparable to those of several repeaters in star-forming galaxies. Therefore, FRBs in both star-forming and old, quiescent hosts can reside in relatively complex magneto-ionic environments, which suggests that FRB sources may form through multiple channels.

papers.title: Playing CHESS with stars II. Homogeneous analysis of high-resolution optical spectra for a sample of 135 giants in 14 bulge globular clusters
papers.summary: Bulge globular clusters are key tracers of the complex formation history of the Galactic bulge, as they retain information on its past star-formation episodes. Their chemical abundances serve as empirical `fossil records'' of the early evolution of the bulge. We present a homogeneous analysis of archival high-resolution UVES spectra for 135 giants in 14 Galactic bulge globular clusters. We explore the results in the context of the phenomenon of multiple stellar populations and discuss what the abundances reveal about the chemical evolution of the bulge. We employed the CHEmical Survey analysis System (CHESS) pipeline to derive atmospheric parameters on an accurate scale defined by reference stars. Abundances for Li, O, Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Sc, Y, Zr, Ba, Ce, Nd, and Eu were derived by spectrum synthesis. Deviations from local thermodynamic equilibrium (i.e., non-LTE or NLTE) were taken into account for Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Y, Ba, and Eu. We serendipitously discovered a Li-rich giant with A(Li) = 1.68 (after 3D NLTE corrections) in NGC 6723, which was hidden in the archival data. Our sample includes both first- and second-generation stars, as indicated by the observed spread in Na abundances. Compared to halo clusters, the bulge clusters show a lower [{\alpha}/Fe] plateau at low metallicity and a more gradual decline in [{\alpha}/Fe] toward higher metallicities. The Sc abundances are below solar and lower than in disk stars of the same metallicity. This difference could be important for solving open questions about the nucleosynthesis of this element. None of the clusters exhibit any significant spreads in heavy elements. Most clusters exhibit [Ba/Eu] \sim 0.0, indicating a contribution from both s- and r-processes. Clusters with [Fe/H] < -0.5 show negative [Ce/Nd] ratios, supporting the idea that these elements were predominantly produced by the r-process in these clusters.

papers.title: Cosmological lensing as a jump process
papers.summary: We develop a jump-process formalism for the probability density function (PDF) of gravitational lensing fields. In the Born approximation, each lens adds a jump to the convergence $\kappa$ and the two components of the shear, making lensing a jump process in redshift. For independent lenses, the joint PDF of the lensing fields obeys a compensated Kolmogorov-Feller equation, which we solve in closed form in Fourier space and extend to clustered lenses using their two-point correlation function. A Fourier-Hankel inversion then yields the joint PDF of $\kappa$ and the shear magnitude $\gamma$, from which the magnification PDF follows, including its high-magnification tail, without sampling noise. We use these PDFs to train an updated version of the FLUMEN emulator, which makes likelihood-based inference from the full magnification distribution feasible across cosmologies. To motivate such analyses, we estimate that samples of $10^4$ Roman supernovae, $10^5$ Rubin supernovae, 300 Einstein Telescope standard sirens, and 12 LISA standard sirens could constrain the matter fluctuation amplitude $\sigma_8$ respectively to 4.8\%, 5.1\%, 8.5\%, and 19\%, with the other cosmological parameters fixed.

papers.title: Six New Eclipsing AM CVn Binaries from the Zwicky Transient Facility
papers.summary: We present the discovery of six new eclipsing AM CVn binaries, helium-accreting ultracompact systems in which a cool donor eclipses the accreting white dwarf. The systems were found in a GPU-accelerated Box Least Squares (BLS) search of Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) photometry and have orbital periods of 39.3 to 59.9 minutes. We obtained spectroscopy with the Low Resolution Imaging Spectrometer (LRIS) on the Keck I telescope for all six systems, and every spectrum shows helium emission with no detectable hydrogen, confirming their AM CVn classification. Our discoveries increase the number of deeply eclipsing AM CVn from 11 to 17 (i.e., systems in which the accreting white dwarf is both the dominant source of optical light and eclipsed by the donor). With high-speed photometric follow-up, these systems will provide the mass ratios, inclinations, and fractional radii of both components. They will also provide new tests of AM CVn formation models and stronger constraints on the long-term evolution of these sources.

papers.title: Measuring Precipitable Water Vapor through Dual-Band GPS at Rubin Observatory
papers.summary: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) in Earth's atmosphere is a known source of systematic error in ground-based astronomical measurements, particularly at wavelengths greater than 7,000 angstroms. PWV produces wavelength-dependent extinction in the spectral energy distributions of observed sources. For high-precision applications, such as supernova cosmology, the transmission function must be measured accurately and precisely for each observation. The Vera C. Rubin Observatory is located in the Chilean Andes, a region known for dry conditions. However, even at this location, time-variable absorption by water vapor is a factor. Signal delays from Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) offer a robust, easy, 24-hour monitoring of PWV. In this paper we present measurements from the first six months of GNSS-PWV at Rubin Observatory. We verified our analysis by replicating results from the International GNSS Service (IGS), demonstrating high consistency. We then installed and commissioned a Trimble Net R9 receiver at Allegheny Observatory for a commissioning run before it was relocated to Rubin Observatory. At Rubin Observatory we have been continuously measuring PWV since 2025 September 5. We find average PWV levels of 3.0 kg/m$^2$ in Southern Hemisphere spring (September to November) and 5.4 kg/m$^2$ in summer (December to February). The PWV at Rubin also has a clear daily variation with an amplitude of 1.2-3.8 kg/m$^2$ that is highly correlated with the east-west wind strength. We conclude that the proposed GNSS-based processing method achieves an accuracy of 0.9 kg/m$^2$ with 0.36 kg/m$^2$ precision, confirming the capability for continuous, high-temporal-resolution PWV monitoring to support demanding LSST science cases.

papers.title: Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys (COMPASS) VIII. First interstellar detection of fully deuterated methyl cyanide
papers.summary: Deuteration is a powerful metric to gain insight into the formation pathways of interstellar molecules in star forming regions. Our primary goal is to search for the fully deuterated form of methyl cyanide, CD3CN, in the ISM. We used a sensitive imaging spectral survey of the protostellar system L1551 IRS5 in the Taurus molecular cloud performed as part of the Large Program carried out with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) called Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys (COMPASS). We derived the column densities of methyl cyanide and several of its less abundant isotopologs, including deuterated ones, under the assumption of local thermodynamic equilibrium. All three deuterated isotopologs of methyl cyanide were detected toward the northern binary component of L1551 IRS5. In particular, we report the first interstellar detection of CD3CN. The measured D/H ratio increases by about half an order of magnitude from one deuterated isotopolog to the next, in a similar way as what was measured for methanol in several other low-mass protostars. This suggests that methyl cyanide predominantly forms like methanol on the surface of dust grains during the cold prestellar phase. However, the measured factor of 2 difference between the D/H ratios of methyl cyanide and methanol may either indicate that gas-phase processes during the warm-up stage contribute approximately equally to the production of methyl cyanide, or that methyl cyanide and its deuterated isotopologs are formed during the prestellar phase at a somewhat earlier time than methanol. Multiply deuterated isotopologs are crucial to understand the formation and inheritance of molecules in the ISM by coupling observations and astrochemical models. Unfortunately, no model has so far investigated the deuteration of methyl cyanide up to the fully deuterated form. [Abridged]

papers.title: Extension and validation of the ZPEKTR code for determining the inclination angles of Be stars
papers.summary: Classical Be stars are non-supergiant B-type stars that rotate at a significant fraction of their critical velocity and are surrounded by equatorial circumstellar discs. Rapid rotation induces stellar oblateness and gravity darkening, making the emergent spectrum dependent on both the stellar parameters and the inclination angle. We assess the reliability of the ZPEKTR code for determining inclination angles across different rotation rates, identify the minimum rotation rate required for reliable estimates, and extend our previous analysis to derive consistent stellar parameters for 21 classical Be stars. We evaluated the method through noise-injection tests on synthetic spectra spanning a broad range of rotational rates and inclination angles. We constructed a grid of gravity-darkened synthetic spectra with ZPEKTR, covering the atmospheric and rotational parameter space of classical Be stars. Stellar and rotational parameters were derived through Q minimisation of the HeI 4388, 4471, and 6678 $\r{A}$ line profiles. We applied the method to 21 classical Be stars using archival BeSOS/PUCHEROS spectra and new observations from the LCO/NRES network. The rotation rate was reliably recovered across the tested inclinations, while inclination estimates improved with increasing rotation rate. Reliable inclination estimates were obtained for V/Vc $\geq$ 0.46. For the observed sample, the derived inclination angles show excellent agreement with independent interferometric measurements, yielding $R^{2}$ = 0.985. ZPEKTR provides a promising spectroscopic method for constraining inclination angles and rotational properties in rapidly rotating massive stars. By accounting for stellar deformation and gravity darkening, it offers a practical alternative to interferometric observations and enables the analysis of larger samples of classical Be stars.

papers.title: On the Proper 3D Modeling of Orbits in Wide Binary Gravity Tests
papers.summary: A gravitationally-bound system of wide binary stars with precise 3D relative displacement $\mathbf{r}$ and velocity $\mathbf{v}$ can allow a Keplerian orbit reconstruction for an assumed gravitational parameter $G$. A sufficiently large sample of such systems can also be used to directly infer $G$ specific to the sample. When the sky-plane angular coordinates are (essentially) exact and the distances to the binary stars are sufficiently precise, the orbit modeling can be readily done using two internal consistency relations provided by the ratio of angular separations in R.A.\ and decl.\ and the physical sky-plane separation $s$ that must be satisfied by any Keplerian orbits. A recent study argued that treating $a$ explicitly free with an empirical prior imposed on it can dramatically change the inference of $G$ in the Chae et al.\ sample of 36 wide binaries. Here I introduce and test a Bayesian MCMC algorithm that allows $a$ to be explicitly free, and find using the $\alpha$-Cen AB - proxima system and the Chae et al.\ sample that the explicit-$a$ algorithm with an observational constraint is fully equivalent to the implicit-$a$ algorithm with an internal consistency relation involving $s$. For the $\alpha$-Cen AB - proxima system, I present orbits in Milgromian (MOND) as well as Newtonian gravity models obtained with the verified algorithms. I show that a recent claim of Newtonian gravity from the Chae et al.\ sample may be a consequence of using arbitrarily enlarged errors for some of $\mathbf{r}$ and/or $\mathbf{v}$. I discuss how wide binaries can be properly analyzed and modeled to probe gravity at low acceleration and test gravity models, including the necessity of deriving individual-specific parameters, the importance of follow-up observations for anomalous systems, and the relevance of Bayesian MCMC approaches.

papers.title: TEMPEST - A modular Python-based thermophysical model for rough, irregularly-shaped airless bodies
papers.summary: Comparing observed and predicted surface temperatures on airless planetary bodies is crucial for interpreting their surface processes, constraining activity, and deriving their surface properties. We present a new tool in this endeavour: TEMPEST (Thermophysical Evolution Model for Planetary Environment Surface Temperatures). It is a modular, open-source Python model for diurnal thermal evolution on irregular bodies. TEMPEST can reproduce non-Lambertian multiple scattering using arbitrary Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Functions (BRDFs) and notably incorporates surface roughness on sub-facet scales through representative sphere-section geometry. The model includes an explicit time-stepping one-dimensional periodic conduction solver influenced by Spencer's thermal model Thermprojrs, and a semi-implicit Crank-Nicolson solver, and can be paired with other thermal solvers. Precomputed look-up tables enable fast application of scattering laws (Lambertian, Lommel-Seeliger, Hapke, or input empirical BRDF data), allowing the user to assess their effects in permanently shadowed regions or partially shadowed terrains. TEMPEST is parallelised, running on personal computers in minutes for thousands of facets and scaling to high-performance servers for models exceeding 100,000 facets. Validation was performed against Thermprojrs in one dimension, against Sorli's Binary Thermophysical Model in three dimensions, and with empirical thermal data from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, showing good agreement in each case. Application to the high-resolution shape-model of 25143 Itokawa shows the importance of self-shadowing and radiative mutual heating in controlling local temperatures. TEMPEST has already been used to analyse data from the Lucy Mission, Galileo, and ground-based observations, and is adaptable to upcoming datasets from targets of missions such as Comet Interceptor and Europa Clipper.

papers.title: UNIONS: Red and blue alignments of DESI DR1 galaxies
papers.summary: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are a dominant source of systematics in weak-lensing cosmological analyses, and direct measurements on spectroscopic samples are the primary source of priors on their amplitude. We measure the IA of galaxies from the first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) as a function of colour, stellar mass, and halo mass, by cross-correlating the DESI spectroscopic catalogues with the weak-lensing shape catalogue of the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS) over up to 2400 deg$^2$. We fit the three-dimensional galaxy-galaxy and galaxy-shape multipoles of the DESI BGS, LRG, and ELG samples, split by colour and stellar mass, with the non-linear linear alignment (NLA) and the tidal alignment and tidal torquing (TATT) models. Halo masses are measured for the BGS red sample from galaxy-galaxy lensing and extended to the LRGs through the resulting stellar-to-halo mass relation. Red galaxies are strongly and radially aligned, but their alignment amplitude is not a single power law of halo mass between $6\times10^{11}$ and $3\times10^{13}\,h^{-1}M_\odot$: it is nearly flat at low mass and rises steeply above a break at $1.3\times10^{13}\,h^{-1}M_\odot$. Massive blue BGS galaxies instead show a tangential alignment, detected at $3.3\sigma$, to our knowledge the most significant detection of a non-zero alignment of blue galaxies to date, while the low-mass blue BGS galaxies and the ELGs are consistent with zero. At our current precision, the data do not favour TATT over NLA.

papers.title: Tailoring Infra-Red Filters for Global Mapping of Enceladus' Thermal Environment
papers.summary: We present the results of an initial study into the feasibility and design of the Enceladus Thermal Mapper (ETM) instrument, designed to provide detailed temperature data for Enceladus, an icy moon of Saturn identified by the Cassini Mission as a prime candidate for astrobiological study due to its subsurface ocean and active cryovolcanism. Building on heritage from previous missions including TechDemoSat-1, Mars Climate Sounder, and Lunar Trailblazer, ETM aims to measure temperature variations across Enceladus' surface, including at the poles during the extreme cold of winter, when they can reach as low as 45 K. Where Cassini provided limited high-resolution flyby data of Enceladus due to its Saturn-centric orbit, ETM, in orbit around the icy moon will offer continuous high-resolution thermal mapping with a 384 x 288-pixel sensor, capable of 80 m/pixel resolution from 150 km altitude. This will improve constraints on the Enceladus' global conductive heat loss, and better characterise and contextualise its active South Polar Terrain. To optimise the instrument's filters for thermal emission measurements, a digital model of the filter assembly was developed. This lightweight, low-power instrument is capable of significantly advancing the understanding of Enceladus' geological behaviour and evaluating its potential habitability by providing comprehensive temperature data essential for interpreting its evolution.

papers.title: Mapping Stellar Obliquity Across Space and Time
papers.summary: The angle between a star's rotational angular momentum vector and the orbital angular momentum vector of its planets---stellar obliquity---encodes the initial conditions and dynamical history of planetary systems. Variations in obliquity with orbital separation may arise from either primordial disk structure (e.g., broken or warped protoplanetary disks with misaligned inner and outer regions) or subsequent dynamical interactions with planets or external perturbers. Comparing obliquities across orbital distance therefore probes the spatial imprint of these processes, while comparisons across age constrain their temporal evolution. To test for signatures of obliquity evolution in both space and time, we compare stellar inclinations with orbital inclinations for 114 single Sun-like stars spanning four samples that probe distinct regimes of orbital separation and age: 49 protoplanetary disk systems, 24 debris disk systems, 21 warm Jupiter systems, and 20 hot Jupiter systems. We find minimum misalignment rates of $33^{+7}_{-6}$% for protoplanetary disk systems, $21^{+9}_{-7}$% for debris disk systems, $23^{+10}_{-8}$% for warm Jupiter systems, and $20^{+9}_{-8}$% for hot Jupiter systems. These rates are consistent within 1$\sigma$ across all samples. The absence of significant variation in minimum-obliquity distributions with either orbital separation or system age suggests that stellar obliquities for Sun-like stars may be largely established at formation with limited subsequent evolution in both space and time. These results are consistent with post-formation inclination evolution being either infrequent, confined to small misalignments, or restricted to regions of parameter space not examined here---such as systems with close stellar companions, hot host stars, small planets, and long-period giant planets.

papers.title: The IRAC Distant Cluster Survey
papers.summary: We present the Infrared Array Camera (IRAC) Distant Cluster Survey (IDCS), a catalog of 825 galaxy cluster and group candidates identified in the Bo\"otes field using the PZWav detection code. Candidates are selected using photometric redshift probability distributions derived from twelve-band optical and infrared imaging. The catalog spans $0.08 < z < 2.0$ (median $z = 0.93$) and includes 147 systems at $z \geq 1.5$. For $z < 1.5$, simulations indicate a purity of $93\%$ at the adopted S/N $\geq 4$ threshold and $50\%$ completeness at $\log(M_{200c}/M_\odot) = 13.74 \pm 0.01$. We validate the cluster photometric redshifts through comparison with spectroscopic data, finding $\sigma_z/(1+z)=0.017$. Including 18 previously published IRAC Shallow Cluster Survey (ISCS) systems, a total of 80 IDCS cluster candidates are now confirmed through spectroscopy and/or X-ray observations. DESI DR1 spectroscopy provides redshifts for 38 systems, including 23 newly confirmed clusters. These DESI-confirmed systems span $0.12 < z < 0.93$ and have at least 10 spectroscopic members each, from which we measure a median velocity dispersion of $\sim 490$ km s$^{-1}$, corresponding to a median halo mass of $1.1 \times 10^{14} M_\odot$. A positional comparison with 39 independently confirmed literature clusters yields a median centroid offset of 211 kpc. The IDCS catalog provides a cluster sample spanning a wide redshift range, with a selection function characterized through simulations and is a valuable resource for studies of large-scale structure, galaxy evolution in dense environments, and the calibration of cluster detection techniques for current and upcoming wide-field surveys, including LSST, Roman, and Euclid.

papers.title: An Empirically Calibrated [C II] Luminosity-Halo Mass Relation for Line Intensity Mapping
papers.summary: Millimeter-wave line intensity mapping aims to observe the high-redshift universe through the 158 $\mu$m fine-structure line of [C II], the brightest far-infrared line of star-forming galaxies. Whether a [C II] experiment at $z>4$ measures the clustering of large-scale structure, which carries rich cosmological information, rather than the shot noise of the emitters depends on the amplitude and the shape of the [C II] power spectrum. Forecasts often build the power spectrum from a halo mass--luminosity relation, $L(M_h)$, chained from scaling relations measured in other regimes or read off simulations, without a quantified uncertainty. We instead calibrate a double power-law $L(M_h,z)$ on [C II] data alone: the mean [C II] intensity from tomographic cross-correlation at $0.4<z<4.2$ and the luminosity-function measurements and limits at $z\simeq0$ and $4.3\lesssim z\lesssim8$. The four parameters of the double power law are fitted at $z=4.5$ and $5.5$ separately, with no assumption about their evolution, and then jointly across $0<z<7$, and we examine how the uncertainty depends on the modeling assumptions. The shape of the power spectrum is settled by the existing data. The clustering peak stands a factor of $45\,(23$-$93)$ and $64\,(38$-$112)$ above the shot-noise floor at $z=4.5$ and $5.5$, and the two cross at $k_c\simeq0.37$ and $0.44\,h$Mpc$^{-1}$. The amplitude is known less well, the clustering power to $0.5-0.6$ dex and the shot noise to $0.7-0.9$ dex. The results show that the signal comes from halos accessible by current galaxy surveys, those that host the Lyman-break galaxies and Ly$\alpha$ emitters at these redshifts. The luminosity-weighted bias is relatively high, with values of $4-5$.

papers.title: The unresolved high-mass frontier of the black hole Fundamental Plane
papers.summary: Accreting black holes follow a Fundamental Plane (FP) linking radio and X-ray luminosities to black hole mass, but whether this relation changes in the ultramassive regime, above $\sim10^{10}\,\Msun$, remains unresolved. Brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) provide the most direct access to this regime, although earlier claims of enhanced radio emission relied largely on heterogeneous nuclear measurements and black hole masses inferred from host-galaxy proxies. We recalibrate the forward FP using galaxies with direct dynamical mass measurements and reassess the evidence for a high-mass radio excess using the available BCG data. We find that the archival proxy-mass sample cannot uniquely establish such an excess because the inferred signal remains sensitive to the mass calibration and radio-selection properties of the sample. Using mock observing programs, we further show that the predictive width measured from existing observations makes a high-mass transition difficult to both detect and localize with present samples. The existing data therefore provide no compelling evidence for a distinct high-mass branch of the FP. Resolving this question will require a substantially larger, uniformly selected sample of galaxies with direct black hole masses and matched, preferably quasi-simultaneous, nuclear radio and X-ray measurements. A focused pilot survey of several dozen direct-mass systems would provide a practical first step toward establishing whether the required precision is achievable.

papers.title: From Dispersion to Metallicity: Probing the Milky Way Circumgalactic Medium with Fast Radio Bursts
papers.summary: Circumgalactic Medium (CGM) plays a critical role in galactic evolution, serving as the primary reservoir for accretion and outflows. In this work, we present a novel statistical analysis to derive CGM metallicity from the dispersion measure (DM) of 25 Fast Radio Burst (FRB) sightlines. By combining metallicity-dependent oxygen absorption DM estimates with metallicity-independent FRB DMs, we directly constrain the metallicity of the hot phase of the Milky Way (MW) CGM. Considering different diffuse baryon fractions ($f_{\text{d}} = 0.0, 0.6, 0.8$) in the Intergalactic Medium (IGM) and intervening halos, the median metallicities of CGM are $Z_{\text{CGM}} = 0.12_{-0.04}^{+0.09} \, Z_{\odot}$, $0.26_{-0.12}^{+0.18} \, Z_{\odot}$, and $0.39_{-0.20}^{+0.26} \, Z_{\odot}$, respectively, by the bootstrapping method. Super-solar metallicity is seen in multiple sightlines for $f_d=0.8$, which is implausible for MW CGM metallicities. Even under conservative lower-bound estimates ($f_{\text{d}} = 0.0$), the inferred CGM metallicity significantly exceeds expectations for IGM accretion ($Z_{\text{IGM}} \lesssim 0.1 \, Z_{\odot}$), providing strong empirical evidence that a large fraction of the metal-enriched galactic feedback material is efficiently retained within the Milky Way CGM. Furthermore, we observe significant sightline-to-sightline variation in inferred metallicities, pointing toward a highly anisotropic multi-phase CGM shaped by complex interactions between feedback outflows and cosmic accretion.
