papers.title: Active STAR-RIS-Aided RSMA IoT Systems: Performance Analysis, Model-Based and Data-Driven Resource Allocation Frameworks
papers.summary: STAR-RISs have emerged as a promising technology for achieving full-space signal coverage with low hardware complexity and energy consumption. In parallel, RSMA offers a flexible interference management mechanism that enhances spectral efficiency and user fairness. Integrating STAR-RIS with RSMA provides strong potential for robust and energy-efficient communications; however, the resulting double-fading cascaded channels and the inherent imbalance between near and far users pose reliability and fairness challenges. This study presents comprehensive information-theoretic and optimization frameworks for active STAR-RIS-assisted RSMA Internet-of-Things systems. Closed-form expressions for the OP and EC are derived under both the presence and absence of direct links. Based on these results, asymptotic OP and EC, diversity order, and array gain are analyzed to characterize system behavior. In addition, throughput-based and spectral-based energy efficiency metrics are investigated to quantify the tradeoffs between transmission performance and power consumption. To enhance user fairness, a fairness-oriented RA framework is developed to jointly optimize power allocation and rate-splitting coefficients using successive convex approximation and block coordinate descent techniques. To further improve scalability and real-time applicability, we introduce a data-driven RA framework based on DMNN, CMNN, and MXGB. This framework approximates the optimization-based solutions with substantially reduced computational complexity. Numerical results show that the proposed MXGB model achieves the shortest execution time while maintaining performance comparable to ground-truth-based benchmarks. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations validate the analytical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed frameworks.

papers.title: Safe Unicycle Navigation Among Multiple Obstacles Under Bounded Disturbances: A Learning-Augmented CLF-CBF Approach (Extended Version)
papers.summary: This paper presents a robust control framework for safe navigation of a unicycle robot to a goal among multiple static obstacles under an unknown, time-varying disturbance. The controller solves a single real-time quadratic program (QP) that combines a goal-reaching term with one safety term per obstacle. The goal-reaching term is a cross-track control Lyapunov function built from body-frame tracking errors rather than a bearing angle, which keeps its Lie derivatives bounded everywhere, including the goal. Safety is encoded using robust control barrier functions, one per obstacle, each tightened by a closed-form, state-dependent disturbance bound. When stabilization and safety conflict, a slack variable relaxes only the convergence requirement, so that the safety constraints remain strictly enforced. Whenever the QP is feasible, the robust barrier constraints guarantee forward invariance of every obstacle's safe set under all admissible disturbances. Complementing this safety guarantee, a Lyapunov analysis yields an explicit ultimate bound on the distance to the goal. A learning-augmented variant replaces the fixed objective with a reinforcement-learning reference, which accelerates convergence when multiple constraints are simultaneously active. We further derive the obstacle separation below which the gap between two obstacles becomes too narrow to pass through under the robust constraints. For such gaps, a learned virtual goal for the Lyapunov function steers the robot around the obstacles without compromising safety. Simulations, a Monte Carlo study, and a comparison against a sampled-data robust baseline support the theoretical results.

papers.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
papers.summary: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.

papers.title: Minimum-Energy Control for Stochastic Linear Systems: A Data-Driven Approach with Finite-Sample Guarantees
papers.summary: The open-loop minimum-energy control (MEC) problem asks for control inputs that minimize the control energy while ensuring the terminal state reaches a desired value. In this paper, we study the open-loop MEC problem for stochastic linear time-invariant systems. We consider a variety of stochastic constraints that enforce the terminal error to be small, and show that Stochastic MEC (SMEC) problem can be formulated as a QCQP. We obtain the optimal solution for SMEC and show that it generalizes the well-known Deterministic MEC problem by introducing novel stochastic variants of controllability and Gramian matrices. When the system dynamics is unknown, we obtain a direct data-driven solution to the SMEC problem using maximum-likelihood estimation and conformal calibration approaches. Finally, we quantify the sub-optimality and constraint violation of our data-driven solutions via finite-sample high-probability upper bounds, and highlight their dependence on the number of experiments, system dimension, and noise-to-signal ratio. We present numerical simulations to validate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Revolutionizing 6G Wireless Networks with RISs: Enhancements in Sensing and Communications
papers.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have emerged as one of the most promising technologies for the next-generation wireless networks, offering advantages such as cost efficiency, low power consumption, flexible deployment, and large effective aperture. Extensive studies have demonstrated the capabilities of RISs to enhance communication performance, including coverage extension, sum-rate improvement, interference suppression, security enhancement, etc. As 6G networks continue to evolve, wireless sensing is expected to play a pivotal role alongside communication. Undoubtedly, RISs possess great potential to enable seamless integration of sensing and communication by supporting both passive and active sensing paradigms. This paper explores how RISs can revolutionize wireless networks by enhancing both communication and sensing capabilities. Specifically, we highlight the fundamental principles, potential applications, and future trends of RIS-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), anticipating that RIS-enabled ISAC will become a key enabler in the upcoming 6G era.

papers.title: Protocol Data Unit Header Decoding and Payload Coding Recovery in the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
papers.summary: Existing Starlink downlink studies describe synchronization, pilots, and predictable waveform elements, but these descriptions do not establish how received header bits specify payload allocations and channel coding. Using 18 frames from one continuous complex-baseband capture spanning approximately 24 ms, we identify two protocol data unit (PDU) header regions in each frame and decode their contents after receiver correction and reference-phase removal. We recover the headers' terminated rate-1/3 convolutional code with constraint length seven and an eight-bit cyclic redundancy check over the concatenated information words. The decoded bits support a conditional 20-bit layout of modulation and coding scheme (MCS) index--length pairs, linking format labels and quantities to subsequent payload regions. Predicted allocation endpoints agree with signal-based estimates in 16 of 18 frames and differ by at most two symbols in the remaining frames. We further recover modulation mappings and equivalent quasi-cyclic low-density parity-check coding relations for several payload formats, including rate-1/2 and rate-5/8 families. Fixed generators predict 78,848, 9,984, and 811,008 parity bits for formats 5, 9, and 21 without disagreement on codewords excluded from their generator fitting. Cross-modulation tests support shared encoders. Formats 28 and 37 have verified shortened cores, with 256 and 384 additional bits unexplained, while format 68 remains unresolved.

papers.title: Safe World Model for Joint Trajectory and Beamforming Design of Mobile Base Stations
papers.summary: Mobile base stations (MBSs), including aerial and ground-based platforms, provide flexible wireless coverage through adaptive positioning. However, jointly optimizing their trajectories and digital beamforming is challenging because movement changes channel conditions and interference, while beamforming determines the resulting signal and interference powers. These coupled decisions also account for how current movements affect future positions and communication performance under mobility and safety constraints. We formulate this problem as a constrained Markov decision process that maximizes the time-averaged sum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), subject to mobility, obstacle region avoidance, and transmit-power constraints. To support long-term planning and reduce the extensive environment interactions required by model-free reinforcement learning, we develop a SafeDreamer-based world model framework that learns latent system dynamics from experience and optimizes a joint trajectory and beamforming policy through imagined trajectories. Feasibility-preserving action mappings and safety cost signals incorporate operational constraints into policy learning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves higher time-averaged sum SINR than the proximal policy optimization and deep Q-network baselines, while exhibiting improved sample efficiency and more reliable constraint satisfaction.

papers.title: Why the Swing Parameters Are Sloppy
papers.summary: When a multi-parameter model is fitted to measured data, only a few parameter combinations are often identifiable, as Fisher Information Matrix eigenvalues span several orders of magnitude. Sensitivity-based tools, including the Fisher Information Matrix and MBAM, reveal this structure analytically, while manifold learning can recover it from sampled trajectories. For an infinite-bus synchronous generator, both approaches show that inertia H and damping D are among the least identifiable parameters on a late post-disturbance window, t in [3,5] s, where six of the eleven parameters suffice to describe the response. We explain this result from the geometry of the dynamics rather than from that of the parameter-to-data map. The rotor swing is a fast fibre that has collapsed onto a two-dimensional normally attracting invariant manifold (NAIM) of the transient fluxes before the window opens. The zeroth-order NAIM is exactly independent of $H$, $D$, $T_{d0}''$ and $T_{q0}''$, four of the five MBAM limits. We prove, under stated smoothness and rank conditions, that each of the four limits is a boundary of the model manifold at a distance equal, to first order in the parameter, to its current profiled speed. The same analysis predicts how identifiability changes with the experiment: neither a larger initial speed deviation nor a load change restores H or D in the late window, whereas the early window [0, 2]s makes H the best-determined parameter. Evaluated in a physical metric fixed by synchrophasor accuracy limits, the late window identifies five parameters rather than six and the early window nine. The spiked-covariance structure of the linearised trajectory map explains why the principal components of whitened, sampled trajectories reproduce the prior-scaled Fisher spectrum, and regression on those components attains the Fisher-predicted recovery error in 113 of 114 parameter scenario pairs.

papers.title: Whittle Index Policy for Three State Collapsing Bandits
papers.summary: Partially observable restless multi-armed bandit models have been studied for dynamic resource allocation problems under uncertainty. This paper analyzes three-state restless multi-armed bandits with partial observability. These are called collapsing bandit problems if the state of an arm (bandit) is perfectly observable when it is scheduled for allocation. The state is not observable when the arm is not scheduled. The planner has a budget constraint on the scheduling decisions in each time slot. The planner's goal is to maximize expected cumulative long term discounted reward. We study the Whittle index policy. To analyze index policy, first the $N$-armed collapsing bandit problem is decoupled into $N$ single arm problems, and convexity and monotonicity of the optimal value function in belief vector are derived using monotone likelihood ratio (MLR) ordering on state transition dynamics and monotone reward structure assumption. We next show that the optimal policy is of threshold type in belief under sufficiency conditions on the model. These sufficiency conditions depend on Lipschitz bound on the value function in the belief. We further prove the indexability for an arm using Lipschitz bound on subsidy sensitivity with minimal restrictive assumption on the transition probability model and discount factor $\beta.$ Our results generalize to three state and strengthen existing results on threshold policy and indexability with weaker model assumptions. We provide index computation algorithm and we present comparison of the Whittle-index, myopic policy and round-robin policies in the simulation study.

papers.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: static problems
papers.summary: We consider the coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections, where trajectory planning and crossing-order decisions are intrinsically coupled, thereby making their simultaneous optimization intractable in practice. To this end, we propose a heuristic based on a hierarchical structure consisting of a series of nonlinear programs (NLP) in the lower level, which optimizes trajectories of each vehicle for a given crossing order, and a high-level heuristic to design new crossing schedules that exploits sensitivity information from the lower-level NLPs. Extensive numerical simulations across a broad range of traffic scenarios demonstrate that our strategy achieves substantially improved scheduling with respect to first-in-first-out ordering while preserving computational tractability.

papers.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: dynamic problems
papers.summary: The coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections requires deciding both the trajectories of the vehicles and their crossing order, with the additional difficulty that the set of vehicles to be coordinated changes as traffic flows through the intersection. Since the resulting mixed-integer optimal control problem is hard to solve online, we propose an arrival-triggered receding-horizon scheme built around a schedule-refinement heuristic: for a fixed crossing order, a single nonlinear program (NLP) optimizes all trajectories and crossing times, and the first-order sensitivities of the cost with respect to the vehicle schedule are used to select adjacent swaps that are likely to reduce the overall cost. Replanning is triggered only when a new vehicle arrives, the new vehicle is appended at the tail of the current crossing order, and a memory of evaluated swaps that persists across replanning steps avoids redundant computations. Simulations of traffic scenarios involving streams of a few hundred heterogeneous vehicles show that the proposed scheme recovers most of the optimality gap incurred by first-in-first-out scheduling.

papers.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: real-time algorithms
papers.summary: When coordinating connected and automated vehicles at an unsignalized intersection, the crossing order and the vehicle trajectories must be decided jointly. For a fixed crossing order, the problem can be formulated conveniently in a bi-level form where each vehicle solves its own optimal control problem, whose optimal value is a function of its entry and exit times, and a coordinator optimizes these times subject to precedence constraints. We compute the first and second order sensitivities of lower-level problems, which are required to solve the upper-level problem, by means of algorithmic differentiation using the real-time software package \texttt{acados}. This implementation exploits tailored algorithms to obtain a computationally efficient implementation of the optimal coordination algorithm. We validate our implementation in numerical simulations that demonstrate both real-time feasibility and effectiveness of our algorithm.

papers.title: Data-driven Wasserstein distributionally robust generalized Nash equilibrium problems with heterogeneous uncertainty
papers.summary: We study stochastic generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems with heterogeneous, stochastic uncertainty in the cost functions. To address the distributional uncertainty, we let each agent construct an individual Wasserstein ambiguity set around an empirical distribution obtained from private data. We establish finite-sample robustness guarantees for any distributionally robust (DR) GNE. Focusing on variational equilibria, we derive a DR variational inequality (VI) reformulation and establish asymptotic consistency with the nominal stochastic game. Under mild conditions, we derive an exact finite-dimensional generalized Nash equilibrium reformulation. We then quantify how heterogeneous worst-case distributions affect monotonicity, and derive conditions for uniqueness and equilibrium sensitivity. To compute a variational DR GNE, we propose an inexact projected method and establish convergence under vanishing oracle errors, an asymptotic error bound under bounded oracle errors, and linear convergence under exact oracle evaluations.

papers.title: A Linear Parameter-Varying Framework for the Analysis of Time-Varying Optimization Algorithms
papers.summary: In this paper we propose a framework to analyze iterative first-order optimization algorithms for time-varying convex optimization. We assume that the temporal variability is caused by a time-varying parameter entering the objective, which can be measured at the time of decision but whose future values are unknown. We consider the case of strongly convex objective functions with Lipschitz continuous gradients under a convex constraint set. We model the algorithms as discrete-time linear parameter varying (LPV) systems in feedback with monotone operators such as the time-varying gradient. We leverage the approach of analyzing algorithms as uncertain control interconnections with integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) and generalize that framework to the time-varying case. We propose novel IQCs that are capable of capturing the behavior of time-varying nonlinearities and leverage techniques from the LPV literature to establish novel bounds on the tracking error. Quantitative bounds can be computed by solving a semi-definite program and can be interpreted as an input-to-state stability result with respect to a disturbance signal which increases with the temporal variability of the problem. As a departure from results in this research area, our bounds introduce a dependence on different additional measures of temporal variations, such as the function value and gradient rate of change. We exemplify our main results with numerical experiments that showcase how our analysis framework is able to capture convergence rates of different first-order algorithms for time-varying optimization through the choice of IQC and rate bounds.

papers.title: Finite-Length Empirical Comparison of Polar, PAC, and Invertible-Extractor Secrecy Codes over the Wiretap BSC
papers.summary: We compare three secrecy-coding schemes for the degraded wiretap binary symmetric channel (BSC) in the finite-blocklength regime: (i) polar wiretap coset codes, (ii) PAC codes used as wiretap coset codes, and (iii) the invertible-extractor (IE) framework of Bellare--Tessaro. Our comparison is empirical and uses a common semantic-secrecy metric (distinguishing advantage). For polar coset codes, we compute Eve's polarized bit-channel capacities (via the Tal--Vardy construction) to obtain explicit finite-length upper bounds on mutual-information leakage, yielding strong secrecy bounds. For PAC coset codes, we prove that Eve's synthesized bit-channels are equivalent to those of polar codes (up to a permutation), so the same leakage bounds apply; we then convert these strong-secrecy bounds into semantic-secrecy guarantees for symmetric wiretap channels. For the IE scheme, we use the closed-form semantic-secrecy bounds already established. Finally, we report finite-length results that jointly characterize (a) semantic-secrecy guarantees against Eve and (b) frame-error-rate performance at Bob. Our simulations indicate that Polar and PAC codes exhibit comparable reliability performance under the considered finite-length settings, while PAC codes retain the same secrecy bounds as Polar codes. More broadly, our results highlight that non-universal designs of wiretap codes provide tighter secrecy guarantees than universal design based on invertible extractors.

papers.title: Reachability-Augmented Dual Dynamic Programming for Optimal Path Parameterization
papers.summary: Optimal path parameterization (OPP) is a fundamental problem for planning trajectories along a prescribed geometric path under kinodynamic constraints and task-dependent objectives. Among existing OPP works, it remains challenging to simultaneously achieve feasibility guarantees, general-objective optimality certificates, and online-compatible computation in a unified framework, especially for third-order OPP (OPP3) with non-convex constraints. This paper proposes reachability-augmented dual dynamic programming (RDDP), a state-grid-free and objective-aware dynamic programming (DP) framework for OPP. The key idea is to replace the relatively complete recourse assumption used in classical dual DP (DDP) with OPP-specific backward reachable sets, and then generate both value-function cuts and trial trajectories only inside these reachable sets. For convex and non-convex OPP, we prove global optimality and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker convergence of RDDP under OPP-specific conditions, respectively. Efficient instantiations are developed for second-order OPP (OPP2) and OPP3. Experiments show that RDDP achieves objective values comparable to convex-optimization baselines with speedups of approximately 15.3 and 4.9 times over the fastest of 4 tested solvers for OPP2 and OPP3, respectively. RDDP also achieves faster convergence than grid-based DP. Compared with reachability-analysis methods, RDDP retains the reachability mechanism while replacing local maximum-control propagation with value-function-guided control selection, thereby enabling objectives beyond traversal time. In summary, RDDP addresses a key capability gap in OPP by unifying certifiable general-objective optimization, reachability-based feasibility preservation, and online-compatible low-dimensional DP computation in a single framework.

papers.title: Continuous-time nonlinear closed-loop in-memory computing for high-accuracy massive MIMO detection
papers.summary: Analog in-memory computing (IMC) has emerged as a promising approach for accelerating matrix operations by exploiting the intrinsic physics of memory arrays. To date, however, most IMC architectures have focused on linear algebra workloads in which computation is encoded in the equilibrium state of a physical system. Extending these principles to nonlinear optimization remains challenging and typically relies on iterative algorithms composed of repeated linear operations. Here, we introduce a continuous-time nonlinear closed-loop IMC architecture for box-constrained zero-forcing (BCZF) decoding in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The proposed architecture embeds the decoding problem directly within the dynamics of a nonlinear feedback network of memory arrays and supply-limited operational amplifiers, allowing solutions to emerge through continuous-time physical optimization. We derive a compact analytical model of the circuit and show that its trajectories minimize an equivalent energy function. Experimental emulation using a fabricated IMC chip confirms the predicted dynamics under realistic hardware nonidealities for up to 16x16 MIMO systems. To overcome the finite precision of analog hardware, we extend mixed-precision iterative refinement from linear algebra to nonlinear continuous-time optimization, enabling reliable detection of high-order modulation formats including 1024-QAM. Benchmark projections indicate operation from ultra-low-energy approximate decoding to high-accuracy massive MIMO detection. Together, these results extend closed-loop IMC from equilibrium-based linear algebra to continuous-time nonlinear optimization and establish a pathway toward efficient physical accelerators for high-accuracy wireless communications.

papers.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
papers.summary: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.

papers.title: Bilinear World Models: Learning Representations with Structured Dynamics for Efficient Control
papers.summary: World models jointly learn latent representations and dynamics that predict how high-dimensional observations evolve under actions. In this work, we propose a JEPA-style world model in which, rather than learning arbitrary latent dynamics, we restrict them to follow a bilinear parameterization. This structure enables efficient planning and control while shifting the modeling burden onto the encoder, encouraging richer representations that expose the controllable geometry of the system. In particular, this structured parameterization allows us to structurally enforce action recoverability, thereby preventing representation collapse by construction. Although prescribing a bilinear parametrization may appear restrictive, we show that a broad class of nonlinear dynamical systems admits a transformation under which the dynamics become bilinear. Empirically, we show across standard 2D and 3D control tasks that representations with bilinear-parameterized dynamics can be learned directly from high-dimensional observations, reducing planning time by nearly three orders of magnitude while retaining or even improving control accuracy. We also propose more demanding regimes of longer-horizon planning and real-time control, and demonstrate that our method succeeds in both, moving JEPA-style world models beyond short-horizon offline planning.

papers.title: From Reconnaissance to Response: Quantitative Risk Parameterization and Game Theoretic Containment in Modern Enterprise Attack
papers.summary: Modern Security Operations Centers struggle with delayed manual incident response, enabling adversaries to advance through the Cyber Kill Chain during early stage reconnaissance. While classical game theoretic defense models optimize strategic resource allocation, they rely on static utility matrices that fail to adapt to dynamic telemetry. This paper presents an integrated, metrics driven decision engine that bridges quantitative risk parameterization and continuous automated response time. Common Vulnerability Scoring Systems exploitability parameters are mapped to attacker success probabilities and evaluate defender log distributions via Factor Analysis of Information Risk Monte Carlo simulations. Real time SIEM logs streams are modeled as Poisson process arrival rates, dynamically updating defender posterior threat belief through sequential Bayesian filtering. A closed form threshold is derived by framing the interaction as a dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game, where the expected unmitigated risk exceeds proactive containment cost. Parameterized against empirical data from the 2023 MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment cyber incident, simulation results demonstrate that the engine suppresses transient background noise while triggering automated SOAR network isolation within seconds of adversarial probing. Multi parameter sensitivity analysis confirms that the decision boundary dynamically adjusts to live perimeter vulnerability, offering a control theoretic foundation for sub minute automated threat containment.

papers.title: CrossEdit: Cross-Modal Training Enables Rich Audio-Visual Editing
papers.summary: Multimedia editing requires generative models to interpret complex, compositional instructions and modify only the desired elements across modalities, a capability largely beyond existing systems. Current approaches are typically limited to simple, single-attribute edits within one modality, since diverse, high-quality editing pairs are hard to obtain, especially for cross-modal tasks where aligned audiovisual (AV) data is scarce. We present CrossEdit, a unified omni-modal editing model for images, audio, and video that performs AV movie scene edits zero-shot through cross-modal transfer. Our key observation is that complex instruction-following, once learned in any modality, generalizes to others. We exploit the additive nature of acoustic signals to procedurally generate large-scale audio editing pairs with compositional instructions, and show that fine-tuning on this synthetic data and self-supervised AV masked reconstruction, alongside a targeted set of curated cross-modal tasks, induces instruction-following that transfers zero-shot to unseen modality and instruction combinations. To evaluate this capability, we release CrossEditBench, a human-annotated benchmark of AV edits on movie scenes, and propose AV-FES, a metric that jointly scores instruction following and consistency. We show that our proposed techniques improve performance on zero-shot AV movie scene editing, while maintaining or improving performance on lip-synced speech editing and standard image, video, and audio editing benchmarks. Demos are available at https://wanchichen.github.io/crossedit/.

papers.title: Context-dependent Runtime Construction of Safe Regions of Attraction from Design-Time Identification for Multi-Candidate Simplex Architectures
papers.summary: Deploying safety-critical cyber-physical systems requires control strategies that reconcile high performance and adaptability with rigorous safety guarantees. Classical control strategies offer stability proofs but are conservative, while advanced optimization- and learning-based controllers achieve high performance but lack formal verification. Runtime Assurance (RTA) architectures bridge this gap by introducing their own (dis-)advantages. Safety filters use online optimization and introduce chattering, while Simplex permissiveness is bounded by the tightness of the certified Region of Attraction (RoA) of its High-Assurance (HA) controller. Targeting this conservatism, we present a two-stage RoA certification procedure leveraging contraction-based stability to establish a target set for Taylor-model-based reachability analysis. We then treat the closed-loop system under HA control as a switched system, enabling: (a) runtime construction of context-dependent safe RoA and (b) safe switching between HA candidates to optimize recovery and maximize the operating envelope of the uncertified High-Performance (HP) controller. We validate this framework on a robotic path-tracking task using a three-stage evaluation: Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) simulation for theoretical verification, high-fidelity Gazebo simulation under unmodeled dynamics, and experiments on physical hardware. Results show that the Simplex architecture maintains safety under fault injection and successfully shields a behavioral-cloning-trained HP controller. Crucially, the decision module introduces negligible overhead (0.028 ms average, 4.13 ms worst-case), consuming under 10 % of the control period.
